messages:
priya-singh: Heads-up — starting onboarding for zephyr-7b-mono (weights pulled from zephyr-org repo). Need a quick license/export-control check before we run quant and infra. TL;DR: is commercial hosting allowed? Any immediate red flags?

mona-legal: @priya-singh can you paste the model license + any downloader/redistribution terms? Also what's the country of origin for the weights? Export controls can depend on that and training data provenance.

priya-singh: license excerpt pasted below:

```
Copyright Zephyr Org 2025
Licensed under Zephyr NonCommercial v1.0
No commercial use or redistribution without separate agreement.
```

mona-legal: yep that's an NC-style license. That basically rules out hosting on our Redwood API or Dedicated for customers. Private on-prem/VPC could be okay if the customer has their own rights — we can't host it ourselves for commercial use.

alejandro-ml: :eyes: Sad. For internal evals we can still run it in the eng-ml sandbox if legal signs off and we don't expose outputs. Do we know if fine-tuning is explicitly forbidden?

mona-legal: NC typically forbids commercial exploitation including fine-tuning for product/features. I need OSS counsel to confirm whether 'non-commercial' is applied to downstream model usage or just redistribution; pinging them now.

license-bot: Link to license: https://repo.zephyr.org/licenses/zephyr-nc-1.0.md :robot_face:

tristan-ops: If legal gives the green light for internal-only eval, I can spin up an isolated VPC with no external egress and HSM-disabled keys. ETA ~1 day to provision.

alejandro-ml: Quant plan: weights are HF fp16. I'll try 4-bit GPTQ and int8 dynamic quant on a single A100 node, then run a small benchmark (NLL/PPL + 50 instruction-following prompts). Will gate any artifacts behind the sandbox.

priya-singh: Can we do a minimal eval run now (no export, no dataset exposure) so we know if quant has reasonable perf?

mona-legal: Internal eval OK under NC as long as outputs aren't served to external users. No hosting, no productization. If counsel later says NC is absolute, we'll have to stop.

alejandro-ml: Understood. I'll add a strict metadata tag to outputs: "internal-only: true" and don't push weights off the cluster. For metrics: NLL, PPL, and instruction accuracy on our 50-prompt set.

priya-singh: Also need provenance check — were any third-party datasets used with additional restrictions (e.g., non-derivative clauses)? @alejandro-ml can you populate the intake sheet provenance fields?

alejandro-ml: Adding fields to intake: [license, weight_origin_url, training_data_licenses, quantizability_notes, fine_tune_allowed_flag, export_control_risk]. Will fill weight checks and dataset licenses tomorrow.

mona-legal: If OSS counsel confirms NC is firm, outcome: block for hosted catalog and Dedicated offerings. We can keep an internal eval record and a note in model-gate that this model is NC-only. If counsel finds it's permissive, we proceed with normal gate flow.

liam-ng: If we hit a commercial gate, consider asking zephyr maintainers for a commercial license/dual-license or CLA. Many projects offer commercial terms if you reach out.

mona-legal: Good idea. I'll prepare a short outreach template that requests a commercial license and clarifies intended use (hosting + paid customers).

priya-singh: Action items summary:
- mona-legal: confirm OSS counsel interpretation and whether fine-tuning/hosting is banned (EOD).
- alejandro-ml: run quant experiments in sandbox and record evals (48h run target).
- tristan-ops: standby to provision isolated VPC if legal allows (1 day).
- liam-ng: assist with outreach template if we need a commercial license.

mona-legal: I'll update the intake row with the legal status and mark as "license-blocked-for-hosting" if counsel confirms NC.

priya-singh: Thanks all — I'll mark intake as blocked for hosting until legal clears. Alejandro, ping here when first evals are up. :thumbsup:

license-bot: Reaction summary: :warning: license flagged as NonCommercial.
